sections.title: Sound of letter ye
paragraphs: The name of this letter is (е) /je/. Its main sound is heard in (ель) /jelʲ/, which means spruce, fir tree. This letter has four sounds. A vowel is a sound made with open air and no touch in the mouth. Stress is the strength you give to one syllable so that it sounds louder and longer.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: First, lift the middle of your tongue close to the roof. Then slide it down into a front mid vowel while spreading your lips. For the second sound, open your mouth slightly and keep your tongue high and forward. For the third sound, start with that quick glide and drop into a short close vowel. For the fourth sound, keep your tongue high and relaxed. Put a hand on your throat to feel it shake.

sections.title: Reading letter ye
paragraphs: When stressed at the start of a word, it makes the sound in (ель) /jelʲ/. When stressed after a vowel, it also sounds as in (поезд) /ˈpo.jist/. When stressed after a consonant, it makes the sound in (лес) /lʲes/ and softens that consonant. When unstressed at the start or after a vowel, it sounds as in (еда) /jɪˈda/. When unstressed after a consonant, it makes the sound in (весна) /vʲɪsˈna/.

sections.title: Common mistakes to avoid
paragraphs: Do not turn the stressed vowel into a long glide like the vowel in day. Keep your mouth steady and do not move your lips at the end. When unstressed, do not say a clear vowel like the sound in bet. Relax your tongue so it becomes short, like the sound in bit.
